name.en: Spring and Autumn and Warring States

events.ja: {r_zheng}は鄢で弟の共叔段の乱を討った。母の武姜に「黄泉に至らずんば相見ること無し」と誓ったが、のちに地下に道を掘って母と再会したという。
events.en: {r_zheng} crushed the revolt of his younger brother Duan at Yan. He swore never to see their mother again "until the Yellow Springs" — and later had a tunnel dug so that he might meet her underground.

events.ja: 周と{n_zheng}は互いに人質を交わした。天子と諸侯が人質を取り交わすのは前代未聞のことで、王室の威信は地に落ちた。
events.en: The Zhou court and {n_zheng} exchanged hostages. That the Son of Heaven should trade hostages with a lord was unheard of, and the royal house lost face.

events.ja: {n_lu}の桓公は夫人を伴って{n_qi}を訪れ、宴の帰りに車中で殺された。斉の襄公が公子彭生に命じたものという。
events.en: Duke Huan of Lu visited {n_qi} with his consort and was killed in his carriage on the way back from a feast — at the order, it was said, of Duke Xiang of Qi.

events.ja: 繻葛の戦い。周の桓王は諸侯を率いて{n_zheng}を討ったが大敗し、鄭の将祝聃の矢が王の肩を射た。天子の権威はこの日に尽きたといわれる。
events.en: At Xuge the Zhou king led the lords against {n_zheng} and was routed; an arrow of the Zheng captain Zhu Dan struck the king in the shoulder. The majesty of the Son of Heaven, it is said, ended that day.

events.ja: {r_chu}は「我は蛮夷なり」と言い放ち、周の許しを待たず自ら王を称した。諸侯の中で王号を名乗った最初の者である。
events.en: {r_chu} declared "I am a barbarian" and, without waiting for Zhou leave, took the title of king — the first of the lords to do so.

events.ja: 紀侯は国を弟に託して去り、{n_ji_state}は{n_qi}に併せられた。九代前の祖先の仇を討ったと{r_qi}は称した。
events.en: The Marquis of Ji left his realm and {n_ji_state} was absorbed by {n_qi}; {r_qi} claimed to have avenged an ancestor nine generations back.

events.ja: {r_chu}は北へ兵を進めて{n_shen}を滅ぼし、県とした。楚が中原へ向かう扉が開いた。
events.en: {r_chu} marched north and destroyed {n_shen}, making it a county. The door from Chu to the Central Plain stood open.

events.ja: {r_chu}は都を郢に移した。郢はのちに四百年、楚の都であり続ける。
events.en: {r_chu} moved the capital to Ying, which would remain the seat of Chu for four centuries.

events.ja: {r_qi}はかつて自分を射た[[p:管仲]]を、[[p:鮑叔牙]]の推挙によって[[a:guanzhong_reform|宰相に迎えた]]。「我を生む者は父母、我を知る者は鮑子なり」と[[p:管仲]]は語ったという。
events.en: {r_qi} made [[p:管仲|Guan Zhong]] — the man who had once shot an arrow at him — [[a:guanzhong_reform|chief minister]], on [[p:鮑叔牙|Bao Shuya]]'s word. "My parents gave me life," [[p:管仲|Guan Zhong]] said, "but it is Bao who knows me."

events.ja: 長勺の戦い。[[p:曹劌]]は{n_qi}の軍が三度太鼓を打つまで動かず、敵の気が尽きたところで討って出て大勝した。「一鼓して気を作し、再びして衰え、三たびして竭く」。
events.en: At Changshao [[p:曹劌|Cao Gui]] held {n_lu}'s men until {n_qi} had beaten the drums three times, then struck and won. "The first drum rouses the spirit, the second dulls it, the third exhausts it."

events.ja: {r_chu}は{n_xi}を滅ぼし、その夫人息嬀を妻とした。夫人は二人の子を産んだが、ついに楚王に言葉をかけなかったという。
events.en: {r_chu} destroyed {n_xi} and took its lady, Xi Gui, as his wife. She bore him two sons, but it is said she never spoke a word to him.

events.ja: {r_qi}は鄄に諸侯を集めて盟を主宰した。諸侯の長「覇者」の始まりである。
events.en: {r_qi} gathered the lords at Juan and presided over their covenant — the first of the hegemons, the "elders of the lords".

events.ja: {r_jin}は翼を攻めて[[p:晋侯緡]]を滅ぼし、宝器を周の釐王に献じて晋の君と認められた。分家の曲沃が本家を呑み込んだのである。
events.en: {r_jin} took Yi, destroyed [[p:晋侯緡|Marquis Min]] of Jin, and bought recognition as lord of Jin with treasures sent to the Zhou king. The cadet branch of Quwo had swallowed the main line.

events.ja: これより曲沃の君は晋公と称した。
events.en: From now on the lords of Quwo styled themselves Dukes of Jin.

events.ja: {r_chu}は{n_deng}を滅ぼした。かつて鄧の人々は「楚を滅ぼすのは今のうち」と諫めたが、鄧侯は耳を貸さなかった。
events.en: {r_chu} destroyed {n_deng}. Its ministers had once begged their lord to strike Chu while he could; he had not listened.

events.ja: {r_jin}は驪戎を討ち、その娘[[p:驪姫]]を連れ帰った。のちの晋の内乱の種となる。
events.en: {r_jin} subdued the Li Rong and brought home their daughter [[p:驪姫|Li Ji]] — the seed of a later civil strife in Jin.

events.ja: {n_chidi}が{n_wey}に攻め入った。鶴を好み、鶴を大夫の車に乗せていた懿公に兵たちは「鶴に戦わせよ」と言い放ち、衛は大敗、都朝歌は落ちた。
events.en: {n_chidi} invaded {n_wey}. Duke Yi had loved cranes so well he gave them officials' carriages; now his soldiers told him to send the cranes to fight. Wey was routed and its capital Zhaoge fell.

events.ja: {r_qi}は{n_yan}の求めに応じて{n_shanrong}を討った。帰路、道に迷った軍は老馬を放ち、その後について道を見出したという。
events.en: {r_qi} answered {n_yan}'s call and marched against {n_shanrong}. Lost on the way home, the army let an old horse go ahead and followed it back to the road.

events.ja: 召陵の盟。{r_qi}は諸侯の軍を率いて{n_chu}に迫り、周への貢ぎ物を怠った罪を問うた。両国は戦わずに盟を結んだ。
events.en: The covenant of Shaoling. {r_qi} led the lords' armies to {n_chu}'s border and charged it with failing its tribute to Zhou; the two made a covenant without a battle.

events.ja: [[p:驪姫]]の讒言により、{n_jin}の太子申生は自ら命を絶った。公子重耳と夷吾は国外へ逃れた。
events.en: Slandered by [[p:驪姫|Li Ji]], Shensheng, heir of {n_jin}, took his own life. The princes Chong'er and Yiwu fled abroad.

events.ja: {r_jin}は{n_yu}に道を借りて{n_guo}を滅ぼした。「唇亡びて歯寒し」との諫めを聞かなかった虞公は、帰り道に軍を返した晋に国を奪われた。
events.en: {r_jin} borrowed the road through {n_yu} to destroy {n_guo}. The Duke of Yu had ignored the warning that "when the lips are gone, the teeth are cold" — the returning army took his realm too.

events.ja: 帰路の晋軍は{n_yu}を滅ぼした。道を貸した礼に受け取った名馬と玉は、晋に戻った。
events.en: On its way home the army of Jin destroyed {n_yu}. The fine horses and jade it had paid for passage came back to Jin.

events.ja: 葵丘の会盟。{r_qi}は諸侯を集め、周王の使者から胙肉を賜った。斉の覇業はここに極まった。
events.en: The covenant of Kuiqiu. {r_qi} gathered the lords and received sacrificial meat from the Zhou king's envoy — the height of Qi's hegemony.

events.ja: {n_qi}の桓公が没すると公子たちは位を争い、桓公の亡骸は六十七日も放置され、蛆が戸口から這い出たという。
events.en: When Duke Huan of {n_qi} died, his sons fought over the throne; his body lay unburied for sixty-seven days, and maggots crawled out under the door.

events.ja: 韓原の戦い。{r_qin}は{n_jin}の恵公を捕らえたが、のちに許して帰した。
events.en: At Hanyuan {r_qin} captured Duke Hui of {n_jin}, then let him go home.

events.ja: {r_qin}は{n_rui}を滅ぼした。
events.en: {r_qin} destroyed {n_rui}.

events.ja: 泓水の戦い。{r_song}は「人の困窮に乗じず」と、{n_chu}の軍が川を渡り陣を整えるのを待ってから戦い、大敗して股に傷を負った。後世これを「宋襄の仁」と笑う。
events.en: At the Hong River {r_song} would not "take advantage of another's distress" and waited until {n_chu} had crossed and formed up. He lost, and was wounded in the thigh. Later ages laughed at "the benevolence of Duke Xiang of Song".

events.ja: 十九年の流浪の末、公子重耳は{r_qin}の兵に送られて{n_jin}に帰り、位に即いた。従者の[[p:介子推]]は恩賞を求めず、母と山に隠れた。
events.en: After nineteen years of wandering, Prince Chong'er returned to {n_jin} escorted by {r_qin}'s soldiers and took the throne. His follower [[p:介子推|Jie Zitui]] asked no reward and hid in the mountains with his mother.

events.ja: {r_wey}は同姓の{n_xing}を滅ぼした。
events.en: {r_wey} destroyed {n_xing}, a house of its own clan.

events.ja: 城濮の戦い。{r_jin}は流浪の頃に楚王と交わした約束を守って「三舎」(九十里)退き、そのうえで{n_chu}の将子玉の軍を破った。続く践土の会盟で晋は覇者となった。
events.en: At Chengpu {r_jin} kept the promise made to the King of Chu in his wandering years and fell back three days' march before he fought — then broke the army of {n_chu}'s general Ziyu. At the covenant of Jiantu that followed, Jin became hegemon.

events.ja: 殽の戦い。{n_zheng}を襲おうとした{n_qin}の軍は、牛を献じて時を稼いだ鄭の商人[[p:弦高]]に企てを見抜かれて引き返し、帰路の殽山で{n_jin}に待ち伏せされ全滅した。
events.en: The battle of Xiao. Qin's army, sent to take {n_zheng} by surprise, was found out by the Zheng merchant [[p:弦高|Xian Gao]], who offered it oxen to buy time; on the way home it was ambushed by {n_jin} in the Xiao hills and destroyed.

events.ja: {r_qin}は[[p:由余]]の策を用いて西戎を討ち、十二の国を併せ千里の地を開いた。周王は金鼓を贈って祝った。
events.en: On [[p:由余|You Yu]]'s counsel {r_qin} subdued the western Rong, adding twelve realms and a thousand li of land. The Zhou king sent bronze drums in congratulation.

events.ja: {r_chu}は三年鳴かず飛ばずと言われた日々を終え、{n_yong}を滅ぼした。「一たび鳴けば人を驚かす」。
events.en: After three years in which, people said, he "neither sang nor flew", {r_chu} destroyed {n_yong}. "Once it sings, it will astonish the world."

events.ja: {r_chu}は兵を洛水のほとりに進め、周の使者に九鼎の大小と重さを尋ねた。使者王孫満は「徳に在りて鼎に在らず」と答えた。
events.en: {r_chu} brought his army to the banks of the Luo and asked the Zhou envoy how large and heavy the Nine Cauldrons were. "It lies in virtue, not in the cauldrons," answered Wangsun Man.

events.ja: 暴君と呼ばれた{n_jin}の霊公が趙穿に殺された。史官董狐は「[[p:趙盾]]その君を弑す」と書き、筆を曲げなかった。
events.en: Duke Ling of {n_jin}, called a tyrant, was killed by Zhao Chuan. The scribe Dong Hu wrote "[[p:趙盾|Zhao Dun]] killed his lord" and would not change a word.

events.ja: {n_chen}の霊公は夏姫のもとに通い、その子夏徴舒に射殺された。
events.en: Duke Ling of {n_chen}, a frequent guest of the lady Xia Ji, was shot dead by her son Xia Zhengshu.

events.ja: 邲の戦い。{r_chu}は黄河のほとりで{n_jin}の大軍を破った。晋兵は舟の縁にすがる味方の指を切り落として逃れ、舟の中の指は掬えるほどであったという。
events.en: At Bi {r_chu} defeated the great host of {n_jin} by the Yellow River. Jin's men in the boats cut off the fingers of comrades clinging to the sides, and the fingers in the boats could be scooped up by the handful.

events.ja: {n_lu}は初めて田の広さに応じて税を取った ([[a:chushuimu|初税畝]])。
events.en: {n_lu} for the first time [[a:chushuimu|taxed land by its area]].

events.ja: 鞍の戦い。{n_jin}の軍が{n_qi}を破った。斉の頃公は御者と衣を取り替えて逃れた。
events.en: At An {n_jin} defeated {n_qi}. Duke Qing of Qi escaped by changing clothes with his charioteer.

events.ja: 楚から亡命した巫臣が{n_wu}に[[a:chariot|戦車]]と弓射の術を伝えた。呉は中原の国々と通じ、楚を背後から脅かし始めた。
events.en: Wuchen, an exile from Chu, taught {n_wu} to fight with [[a:chariot|chariots]] and bows. Wu opened ties with the Central Plain and began to threaten Chu from behind.

events.ja: 宋の華元の仲立ちで、{n_jin}と{n_chu}は兵を収める盟を結んだ。
events.en: Through the mediation of Hua Yuan of Song, {n_jin} and {n_chu} swore to lay down arms.

events.ja: 鄢陵の戦い。{n_jin}は{n_chu}を破り、楚の共王は目に矢を受けた。
events.en: At Yanling {n_jin} defeated {n_chu}; King Gong of Chu was struck in the eye by an arrow.

events.ja: {r_qi}は東方の{n_lai}を滅ぼし、海辺の地を手に入れた。
events.en: {r_qi} destroyed {n_lai} in the east and won the coast.

events.ja: {n_qi}の重臣崔杼が荘公を殺した。太史が「崔杼その君を弑す」と書くと崔杼は太史を殺し、その弟たちも同じく書いて殺され、なお末の弟が同じ文を書いたので、崔杼はついに諦めた。
events.en: Cui Zhu, a great minister of {n_qi}, killed Duke Zhuang. The court scribe wrote "Cui Zhu killed his lord"; Cui killed him, then his brothers who wrote the same — and when the youngest wrote it again, Cui gave up.

events.ja: 弭兵の会。宋の向戌の呼びかけで、{n_jin}と{n_chu}をはじめ諸侯が宋に集まり、兵を収めることを誓った。以後四十年、中原の大戦は途絶えた。
events.en: The covenant to end war. At the call of Xiang Xu of Song, {n_jin}, {n_chu} and the lords met in Song and swore to lay down arms; for forty years the great wars of the Central Plain ceased.

events.ja: {n_zheng}の[[p:子産]]は[[a:written_law|刑法を鼎に鋳込んで]]民に示した。晋の[[p:叔向]]は「民が法を知れば争いの元になる」と非難した。
events.en: [[p:子産|Zichan]] of {n_zheng} [[a:written_law|cast the laws on bronze cauldrons]] for all to see. [[p:叔向|Shuxiang]] of Jin objected that a people who know the law will quarrel over it.

events.ja: {r_chu}は章華台を築いた。細い腰の者を好んだので、宮中には食を断って痩せる者が相次いだという。
events.en: {r_chu} built the Zhanghua terrace. Because he liked slender waists, people at court starved themselves thin.

events.ja: {n_lu}の昭公は三桓 (季孫・叔孫・孟孫の三家) を除こうとして敗れ、斉へ逃れた。
events.en: Duke Zhao of {n_lu} tried to break the Three Huan families (Jisun, Shusun and Mengsun), failed, and fled to Qi.

events.ja: {r_wu}は川をせき止めて{n_xu_h}の都を水攻めにし、これを滅ぼした。
events.en: {r_wu} dammed a river to flood the capital of {n_xu_h}, and destroyed it.

events.ja: 柏挙の戦い。[[p:孫武]]と[[p:伍子胥]]に率いられた{n_wu}の軍が{n_chu}を破り、都の郢に入った。[[p:伍子胥]]は平王の墓をあばき、その屍を三百回鞭打ったという。
events.en: At Boju the army of {n_wu}, led by [[p:孫武|Sun Wu]] and [[p:伍子胥|Wu Zixu]], broke {n_chu} and entered its capital Ying. [[p:伍子胥|Wu Zixu]], it is said, dug up King Ping's body and flogged it three hundred times.

events.ja: 楚の[[p:申包胥]]は{n_qin}の宮廷の庭で七日七晩泣き続け、ついに援軍を得た。秦の兵に追われて{n_wu}は郢から引き揚げた。
events.en: [[p:申包胥|Shen Baoxu]] of Chu wept in the courtyard of {n_qin} for seven days and nights until he was given an army. Pressed by Qin, {n_wu} withdrew from Ying.

events.ja: 夾谷の会。[[p:孔子]]は{n_lu}の定公の相として{n_qi}との会盟に臨み、斉の企てを退けて奪われていた土地を返させた。
events.en: At the meeting of Jiagu [[p:孔子|Confucius]] attended Duke Ding of {n_lu} and thwarted a plot of {n_qi}, winning back land Qi had taken.

events.ja: 檇李の戦い。{n_yue}の[[p:句践]]は罪人を陣の前に並ばせて自ら首を刎ねさせ、呉兵が呆然とする隙を突いて大勝した。呉王[[p:闔閭]]は足の指を射られ、その傷がもとで没した。
events.en: At Zuili [[p:句践|Goujian]] of {n_yue} had condemned men march out before his lines and cut their own throats; while the men of Wu stared, Yue struck and won. King [[p:闔閭|Helü]] of Wu, hit in the toe, died of the wound.

events.ja: 夫椒の戦い。父の仇を忘れぬよう薪の上に臥した{r_wu}は{n_yue}を破り、会稽山に追い詰められた[[p:句践]]は臣従を誓った。[[p:句践]]は苦い肝を嘗めて恥を忘れまいとしたという (臥薪嘗胆)。
events.en: At Fujiao the King of Wu — who had slept on firewood so as never to forget his father's death — broke {n_yue}. Cornered on Mount Kuaiji, [[p:句践|Goujian]] swore submission, and tasted gall every day so as never to forget the shame.

events.ja: 艾陵の戦い。{n_wu}が{n_qi}の大軍を破った。同じ年、諫め続けた[[p:伍子胥]]は剣を賜って自害し、「我が目を東門に懸けよ、越の軍が呉に入るのを見よう」と言い残した。
events.en: At Ailing {n_wu} crushed the army of {n_qi}. The same year [[p:伍子胥|Wu Zixu]], who would not stop warning his king, was handed a sword to kill himself: "Hang my eyes on the east gate, so they may watch the army of Yue march in."

events.ja: 黄池の会で{r_wu}が晋と覇を争っている間に、{n_yue}は呉の都を襲った。
events.en: While {r_wu} contended with Jin for the hegemony at Huangchi, {n_yue} fell upon Wu's capital.

events.ja: {n_lu}の西の狩りで麒麟が捕らえられた。[[p:孔子]]は「吾が道窮まれり」と嘆き、『春秋』の筆を擱いたという。
events.en: A qilin was caught in a hunt west of {n_lu}. "My way has come to its end," [[p:孔子|Confucius]] lamented, and laid down the brush of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

events.ja: {n_qi}の田常 (陳恒) が簡公を殺し、国政を握った。田氏が斉を奪う日が近づいた。
events.en: Tian Chang of {n_qi} killed Duke Jian and took the government in hand. The day the Tian would take Qi drew near.

events.ja: {r_chu}は{n_chen}を滅ぼし、県とした。
events.en: {r_chu} destroyed {n_chen} and made it a county.

events.ja: {r_yue}は{n_wu}を滅ぼした。[[p:夫差]]は「[[p:伍子胥]]に合わせる顔がない」と言って顔を覆い、自害した。功臣[[p:范蠡]]は「狡兎死して走狗烹らる」と書き残して去った。
events.en: {r_yue} destroyed {n_wu}. [[p:夫差|Fuchai]] covered his face — "I cannot look [[p:伍子胥|Wu Zixu]] in the eye" — and killed himself. The minister [[p:范蠡|Fan Li]] left, writing that "when the cunning hare is dead, the hound is cooked".

events.ja: 晋陽の戦い。{n_jin}の重臣智伯は趙氏の晋陽を水攻めにしたが、韓・魏が寝返り、趙・韓・魏の三家に滅ぼされた。[[p:豫譲]]は主君智伯の仇を討とうと、身に漆を塗り炭を呑んで[[p:趙襄子]]を狙った。
events.en: The battle of Jinyang. Zhi Bo, first minister of {n_jin}, flooded Jinyang, the Zhao stronghold — but Han and Wei turned on him and the three houses destroyed him. [[p:豫譲|Yu Rang]] lacquered his skin and swallowed coals to stalk [[p:趙襄子|Zhao Xiangzi]] for his lord's sake.

events.ja: {r_chu}は{n_cai}を滅ぼした。
events.en: {r_chu} destroyed {n_cai}.

events.ja: {r_chu}は{n_qi_state}を滅ぼした。「杞憂」の言葉だけが後に残った。
events.en: {r_chu} destroyed {n_qi_state}, of which only a saying remained: the man of Qǐ who feared the sky would fall.

events.ja: {r_chu}は東の{n_ju}を滅ぼした。
events.en: {r_chu} destroyed {n_ju} in the east.

events.ja: {r_qin}は都を雍に移した。以後三百年、雍は秦の都であった。
events.en: {r_qin} moved the capital to Yong, the seat of Qin for the next three centuries.

events.ja: {n_jin}の[[p:荀林父]]は{n_chidi}の潞氏を滅ぼし、晋は太行山の東西にまたがる大国となった。
events.en: [[p:荀林父|Xun Linfu]] of {n_jin} destroyed the Lu clan of {n_chidi}, and Jin spread across both sides of the Taihang mountains.

events.ja: {n_jin}の荀呉は[[a:chariot|戦車]]を降りて歩兵の隊列を組み、大原で狄を破った。
events.en: Xun Wu of {n_jin} had his men leave their [[a:chariot|chariots]] and fight on foot, and beat the Di at Dayuan.

events.ja: 邯鄲は{n_jin}の趙氏一族の邑となった。
events.en: Handan became a town of the Zhao clan of {n_jin}.

events.ja: {r_wu}は[[p:伍子胥]]に大きな城を築かせ、都を姑蘇に定めた。
events.en: {r_wu} had [[p:伍子胥|Wu Zixu]] build a great walled city and made Gusu the capital.

events.ja: {r_qin}は東へ進むため都を櫟陽に移した。
events.en: {r_qin} moved the capital east to Yueyang.

events.ja: {r_zhao}は都を邯鄲に移した。
events.en: {r_zhao} moved the capital to Handan.

events.ja: {r_wei}は秦の圧力を避けて都を大梁に移した。以後、魏は「梁」とも呼ばれる。
events.en: {r_wei}, pressed by Qin, moved the capital to Daliang; Wei was called "Liang" from then on.

events.ja: {r_chu}は群舒を討ち、その地を併せた。
events.en: {r_chu} subdued the Shu peoples and took their land.

events.ja: {r_chu}は{n_huang}を滅ぼした。
events.en: {r_chu} destroyed {n_huang}.

events.ja: {n_yong}を滅ぼした{r_chu}に、群蛮の諸族も従った。
events.en: With {n_yong} destroyed, the Man peoples too submitted to {r_chu}.

events.ja: {r_cai}は{n_shen_c}を滅ぼした。
events.en: {r_cai} destroyed {n_shen_c}.

events.ja: {r_zheng}は{n_xu}を滅ぼした。
events.en: {r_zheng} destroyed {n_xu}.

events.ja: 淮水の下流の夷の諸族は{n_wu}に従った。
events.en: The Yi peoples of the lower Huai came under {n_wu}.

events.ja: {r_song}は{n_cao}を滅ぼし、[[p:曹伯陽]]を捕らえた。
events.en: {r_song} destroyed {n_cao} and captured its lord, [[p:曹伯陽|Earl Yang]].

events.ja: 長く楚に従ってきた{n_sui}は、楚の県となった。
events.en: {n_sui}, long a follower of Chu, became a county of Chu.

events.ja: {r_jin}は白狄の諸邑 (肥・鼓など) を次々に滅ぼした。
events.en: {r_jin} destroyed one White Di town after another.

events.ja: {r_song}は{n_teng}を滅ぼした。
events.en: {r_song} destroyed {n_teng}.

events.ja: {r_chu}は[[p:孟子]]の故郷{n_zhu}を併せた。
events.en: {r_chu} absorbed {n_zhu}, the home of [[p:孟子|Mencius]].

events.ja: [[a:hufu|胡服騎射]]の騎兵を得た{r_zhao}は、北の林胡・楼煩を討って雲中・雁門の地を開いた。
events.en: With his new [[a:hufu|horse archers]] {r_zhao} struck the Linhu and Loufan in the north and opened the lands of Yunzhong and Yanmen.

events.ja: {n_yan}の将秦開は東胡を千里のかなたへ退け、長城を築いた。
events.en: Qin Kai, a general of {n_yan}, drove the Donghu back a thousand li and built a long wall.

events.ja: {r_qin}の母宣太后は義渠王を甘泉宮に誘って殺し、秦は義渠を滅ぼした。
events.en: The Queen Dowager Xuan of {n_qin} lured the King of Yiqu to the Ganquan palace and had him killed; Qin destroyed Yiqu.

events.ja: 周の[[p:威烈王]]は晋の三卿、韓・趙・魏を諸侯と認めた。{n_jin}は三つに分かれ、戦国の世が始まる。
events.en: [[p:威烈王|King Weilie]] of Zhou recognised the three great ministers of Jin — Han, Zhao and Wei — as lords. {n_jin} split in three, and the age of the Warring States began.

events.ja: {r_wei}は[[p:李悝]]を用いて田を尽くす教えと[[a:li_kui_reform|『法経』]]を定め、[[p:呉起]]に精兵「[[a:wuzu|武卒]]」を鍛えさせた。魏は戦国の初めの最強国となった。
events.en: {r_wei} put [[p:李悝|Li Kui]] in charge — farming to the utmost and [[a:li_kui_reform|a code of law]] — and had [[p:呉起|Wu Qi]] train [[a:wuzu|picked soldiers]]. Wei became the first great power of the Warring States.

events.ja: 田和が周王から斉侯と認められた。太公望以来の姜氏の斉は終わり、{n_qi}は田氏の国となった。
events.en: Tian He was recognised by the Zhou king as Marquis of Qi. The Qi of the Jiang house, descended from the Grand Duke, ended; {n_qi} now belonged to the Tian.

events.ja: {r_chu}は[[p:呉起]]を令尹とし、[[a:wu_qi_reform|貴族の特権を削って]]兵を強めた。翌年、悼王の死とともに[[p:呉起]]は貴族たちに射殺された。王の亡骸に覆い被さった[[p:呉起]]を射た者たちは、のちに罪を問われた。
events.en: {r_chu} made [[p:呉起|Wu Qi]] chief minister, and [[p:呉起|Wu Qi]] [[a:wu_qi_reform|cut the nobles' privileges]] to strengthen the army. When the king died the next year the nobles shot [[p:呉起|Wu Qi]] down — he had thrown himself over the king's body, and those whose arrows struck the corpse were punished for it.

events.ja: {r_han}は{n_zheng}を滅ぼし、都を新鄭に移した。
events.en: {r_han} destroyed {n_zheng} and moved its capital to Xinzheng.

events.ja: 最後の晋公が廃され、{n_jin}の祀りは絶えた。
events.en: The last Duke of Jin was deposed, and the sacrifices of {n_jin} ceased.

events.ja: {r_qin}は[[p:商鞅]]を用いて[[a:shang_yang_reform|変法]]を行った。五家・十家を組にして互いに監視させ、[[a:qin_rank|戦の手柄で爵位を与えた]]。法を信じさせるため、都の南門の木を北門に移した者に五十金を与えたという。
events.en: {r_qin} carried out [[p:商鞅|Shang Yang]]'s [[a:shang_yang_reform|reforms]]: households grouped in fives and tens to watch each other, [[a:qin_rank|ranks given for heads taken in battle]]. To make the people trust the law, he paid fifty gold to the man who carried a pole from the south gate to the north.

events.ja: {r_qin}は都を咸陽に移し、県を置き、田の区画を改めた ([[a:shang_yang_reform|第二次変法]])。
events.en: {r_qin} moved the capital to Xianyang, set up counties and redrew the fields ([[a:shang_yang_reform|the second reform]]).

events.ja: 桂陵の戦い。{n_wei}の[[p:龐涓]]が趙の邯鄲を囲むと、{n_qi}の[[p:孫臏]]は邯鄲ではなく魏の都を突き、引き返す魏軍を待ち伏せて破った (囲魏救趙)。
events.en: At Guiling, when [[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]] of {n_wei} besieged Handan, [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]] of {n_qi} struck not Handan but Wei's own capital, and ambushed the Wei army as it hurried home ("besiege Wei to save Zhao").

events.ja: 馬陵の戦い。[[p:孫臏]]は毎日かまどの数を減らして逃げるふりをし、追う[[p:龐涓]]を馬陵の狭い道に誘い込んだ。「[[p:龐涓]]この樹の下に死す」と記した木の下で[[p:龐涓]]は自害した。
events.en: At Maling [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]] made fewer cooking fires each night, as if his men were deserting, and drew [[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]] into a narrow pass. Under a tree on which [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]] had written "[[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]] dies beneath this tree", [[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]] killed himself.

events.ja: [[p:商鞅]]は旧友の魏の公子卬を会盟に招いて捕らえ、{n_wei}から河西の地を奪った。
events.en: [[p:商鞅|Shang Yang]] invited his old friend Prince Ang of {n_wei} to a parley, seized him, and took the lands west of the Yellow River.

events.ja: 後ろ盾の孝公が没すると[[p:商鞅]]は謀反の罪に問われた。逃れて宿を求めたが「商君の法で、証のない客は泊められぬ」と断られ、捕らえられて車裂きにされた。
events.en: When his patron Duke Xiao died, [[p:商鞅|Shang Yang]] was accused of treason. Fleeing, he sought a bed at an inn and was turned away — "by Lord Shang's law, no guest without papers" — and was caught and torn apart by chariots.

events.ja: 徐州で{r_qi}と{r_wei}は互いを王と認め合った (徐州相王)。
events.en: At Xuzhou {r_qi} and {r_wei} acknowledged each other as kings.

events.ja: {r_chu}は{n_yue}を破り、呉の故地を併せた。越の王族は海辺に散って小さな君長となった。
events.en: {r_chu} defeated {n_yue} and took the old lands of Wu; the house of Yue scattered along the coast as petty chiefs.

events.ja: [[p:蘇秦]]は六国を説いて回り、秦に対する「合従」の盟を結ばせ、六国の相の印を帯びたという。
events.en: [[p:蘇秦|Su Qin]] went from court to court and won the six realms to an alliance against Qin — the Vertical Alliance — and carried, it is said, the seals of chief minister of all six.

events.ja: {r_qin}は王を称した。
events.en: {r_qin} took the title of king.

events.ja: 韓・趙・燕などの君も相次いで王を称した (五国相王)。
events.en: The lords of Han, Zhao, Yan and others took the title of king in turn.

events.ja: {r_qin}は[[p:司馬錯]]を遣わして{n_shu}を滅ぼした。豊かな蜀の地は秦の米蔵となった。
events.en: {r_qin} sent [[p:司馬錯|Sima Cuo]] to destroy {n_shu}. The rich Shu basin became Qin's granary.

events.ja: 続いて{r_qin}は{n_ba}も併せた。
events.en: Next {r_qin} took {n_ba} as well.

do.ja: 子之の乱と斉の燕侵攻
do.en: the Zizhi troubles and Qi's invasion of Yan

events.ja: {n_yan}の王噲は堯舜にならって宰相子之に国を譲り、国は乱れた。{n_qi}はこれに乗じて燕に攻め入った。
events.en: [[p:燕王噲|King Kuai]] of {n_yan}, copying the sage kings, gave his realm to his minister Zizhi, and the country fell into chaos. {n_qi} seized the moment and invaded Yan.

events.ja: {r_yan}は「まず隗より始めよ」との[[p:郭隗]]の言を容れ、黄金台を築いて天下の賢者を招いた。[[p:楽毅]]・[[p:鄒衍]]らが燕に集まった。
events.en: {r_yan} took [[p:郭隗|Guo Wei]]'s advice — "begin with me, Wei" — and built the Golden Terrace to welcome the able men of the world. [[p:楽毅|Yue Yi]], [[p:鄒衍|Zou Yan]] and others came to Yan.

events.ja: {r_chu}は[[p:張儀]]に「斉と絶てば商於の地六百里を献ずる」と欺かれ、怒って{n_qin}と戦ったが、丹陽で大敗して漢中を失った。
events.en: {r_chu}, tricked by [[p:張儀|Zhang Yi]]'s promise of six hundred li if he broke with Qi, made war on {n_qin} in anger — and lost at Danyang, and with it Hanzhong.

events.ja: {r_zhao}は「[[a:hufu|胡服騎射]]」を命じ、遊牧の民の服を着て馬上から弓を射る騎兵を育てた。反対する重臣たちを王は自ら説き伏せた。
events.en: {r_zhao} ordered "[[a:hufu|barbarian dress and mounted archery]]": trousers instead of robes, and bowmen on horseback. He talked round the elders who objected himself.

events.ja: {n_chu}の懐王は会盟に招かれて{n_qin}に入り、そのまま捕らわれた。三年後、懐王は秦で没した。楚の人々は哀れみ、[[p:屈原]]はその死を悼んだ。
events.en: King Huai of {n_chu} went to a meeting in {n_qin} and was held there. He died in Qin three years later, mourned by the people of Chu — and by [[p:屈原|Qu Yuan]].

events.ja: {r_zhao}は中山 ({n_xianyu}) を滅ぼした。
events.en: {r_zhao} destroyed Zhongshan ({n_xianyu}).

events.ja: 伊闕の戦い。秦将[[p:白起]]は{n_han}・{n_wei}の連合軍を破り、首を斬ること二十四万と伝えられる。
events.en: At Yique the Qin general [[p:白起|Bai Qi]] broke the allied armies of {n_han} and {n_wei}; two hundred and forty thousand heads were taken, the records say.

events.ja: {r_qi}は「桀宋」と呼ばれた{n_song}の王偃を討ち、宋を滅ぼした。だが斉の強大化は諸国を恐れさせた。
events.en: {r_qi} struck down [[p:宋王偃|King Yan]] of {n_song} — "the Jie of Song" — and destroyed Song. Qi's new might frightened every court.

events.ja: 済西の戦い。燕の[[p:楽毅]]は秦・韓・趙・魏の兵をあわせて{n_qi}を破り、都臨淄を落として七十余城を取った。残ったのは莒と即墨だけであった。
events.en: At Jixi [[p:楽毅|Yue Yi]] of Yan, with Qin, Han, Zhao and Wei, broke {n_qi}, took Linzi and seventy towns. Only Ju and Jimo held out.

events.ja: 即墨の[[p:田単]]は、角に刃を縛り尾に火をつけた千頭の牛を夜に放って燕の陣を突き崩し、失った城をすべて取り戻した (火牛の計)。
events.en: At Jimo [[p:田単|Tian Dan]] loosed a thousand oxen in the night, blades tied to their horns and fire to their tails, broke the Yan camp, and won back every lost town.

events.ja: 澠池の会。{r_qin}は{r_zhao}に瑟を弾かせて辱めたが、[[p:藺相如]]は秦王に缶を打たせて返した。和氏の璧を完うして帰った[[p:藺相如]]は上卿となり、[[p:廉頗]]とは「刎頸の交わり」を結んだ。
events.en: At Mianchi {r_qin} shamed {r_zhao} by making him play the zither; [[p:藺相如|Lin Xiangru]] made the King of Qin beat a clay pot in return. Lin, who had brought the jade of He home whole, became first minister and swore with [[p:廉頗|Lian Po]] a friendship "unto the cutting of throats".

events.ja: 秦将[[p:白起]]は{n_chu}の都郢を落とし、歴代の王墓を焼いた。楚は東の陳へ都を移した。[[p:屈原]]はこの報を聞いて汨羅に身を投げた。
events.en: [[p:白起|Bai Qi]] of Qin took Ying, the capital of {n_chu}, and burned the royal tombs. Chu moved east to Chen. Hearing the news, [[p:屈原|Qu Yuan]] drowned himself in the Miluo.

events.ja: {r_qin}は[[p:范雎]]の「遠交近攻」の策を用い、遠い斉と結んで近い韓・魏を攻めることにした。
events.en: {r_qin} took up [[p:范雎|Fan Ju]]'s policy of "befriend the far, strike the near": peace with distant Qi, war on neighbouring Han and Wei.

events.ja: 秦に攻められた{n_han}の上党は、秦に降るより趙につくことを選んだ。趙は上党を受け入れ、秦との大戦が避けられなくなった。
events.en: Rather than yield to Qin, the Shangdang commandery of {n_han} gave itself to Zhao. Zhao accepted, and a great war with Qin became certain.

events.ja: 長平の戦い。{n_zhao}は老将[[p:廉頗]]を退け、兵書には通じるが戦を知らぬ[[p:趙括]]を将とした。[[p:白起]]は趙軍を包囲して兵糧を断ち、降った四十万を穴埋めにしたと伝えられる。
events.en: Changping. {n_zhao} replaced the old general [[p:廉頗|Lian Po]] with [[p:趙括|Zhao Kuo]], who knew the books but not war. [[p:白起|Bai Qi]] surrounded and starved the Zhao army, and buried alive the four hundred thousand who surrendered, it is said.

events.ja: 秦軍が邯鄲を囲んだ。[[p:平原君]]は自ら売り込んだ[[p:毛遂]]を伴って楚の援軍を得、魏の[[p:信陵君]]は王の兵符を盗み出して出兵し、ついに秦軍を退けた。[[p:白起]]は出陣を拒んで死を賜った。
events.en: Qin besieged Handan. [[p:平原君|Lord Pingyuan]] won Chu's help with [[p:毛遂|Mao Sui]], who had put himself forward; [[p:信陵君|Lord Xinling]] of Wei stole his king's tally to march his army — and Qin was driven off. [[p:白起|Bai Qi]], who had refused the command, was ordered to die.

events.ja: {r_qin}は{n_zhou}を滅ぼし、九鼎を咸陽へ移した。八百年続いた周の王統はここに絶えた。
events.en: {r_qin} put an end to {n_zhou} and carried off the Nine Cauldrons to Xianyang. The royal line of Zhou, eight centuries old, was gone.

events.ja: {r_chu}は{n_lu}を滅ぼした。周公旦以来の魯の祀りは絶えた。
events.en: {r_chu} destroyed {n_lu}; the line of the Duke of Zhou was gone.

events.ja: 魏の[[p:信陵君]]は五国の兵を率いて河外で{n_qin}を破り、函谷関まで追った。
events.en: [[p:信陵君|Lord Xinling]] of Wei led the armies of five realms, defeated {n_qin} beyond the River and chased it to the Hangu pass.

events.ja: 最後の合従が函谷関で敗れると、{r_chu}は都を寿春へ移した。
events.en: When the last alliance against Qin failed at the Hangu pass, {r_chu} moved the capital to Shouchun.

events.ja: {r_qin}は他国出身の客卿を追い出そうとしたが、[[p:李斯]]の「諫逐客書」を読んで命を撤回した。
events.en: {r_qin} ordered all foreign-born officials out, but withdrew the order on reading [[p:李斯|Li Si]]'s memorial against it.

events.ja: 秦王は[[p:韓非]]の書を読んで「この人と交われるなら死んでも恨まぬ」と言ったが、使者として来た[[p:韓非]]は[[p:李斯]]らに讒され、獄中で毒を仰いだ。
events.en: Reading [[p:韓非|Han Fei]], the King of Qin said he would die content if he could meet the man. When [[p:韓非|Han Fei]] came as an envoy, [[p:李斯|Li Si]] slandered him, and he took poison in prison.

events.ja: 秦の内史騰が{n_han}を攻め、[[p:韓王安]]を捕らえた。六国のうち最初に滅んだのは韓であった。
events.en: The Qin official Teng attacked {n_han} and captured [[p:韓王安|King An]]. Han was the first of the six to fall.

events.ja: 名将[[p:李牧]]が讒言で殺されると、[[p:王翦]]は邯鄲を落とし、{n_zhao}の[[p:幽繆王]]を捕らえた。
events.en: Once the great general [[p:李牧|Li Mu]] had been slandered and killed, [[p:王翦|Wang Jian]] took Handan and captured the King of {n_zhao}.

events.ja: [[p:荊軻]]は易水のほとりで「風蕭蕭として易水寒し、壮士一たび去りて復た還らず」と歌って旅立ち、地図に匕首を隠して秦王に迫ったが、柱をめぐって逃げる王を刺し損ねて斬られた。
events.en: By the River Yi [[p:荊軻|Jing Ke]] sang "The wind sighs, the Yi is cold; the hero goes, and does not return," set out, and came before the King of Qin with a dagger rolled in a map. The king fled round a pillar; [[p:荊軻|Jing Ke]] missed, and was cut down.

events.ja: [[p:王賁]]は黄河の水を引いて大梁を三か月水攻めにし、{n_wei}を滅ぼした。
events.en: [[p:王賁|Wang Ben]] flooded Daliang with the Yellow River for three months and destroyed {n_wei}.

events.ja: 若い李信が二十万で敗れたのち、老将[[p:王翦]]は六十万を率いて{n_chu}を討ち、楚王[[p:負芻]]を捕らえた。「楚は三戸と雖も、秦を亡ぼすは必ず楚ならん」と人々は言った。
events.en: After young Li Xin failed with two hundred thousand, the old general [[p:王翦|Wang Jian]] led six hundred thousand against {n_chu} and captured its king. "Though Chu be but three households," people said, "it is Chu that will destroy Qin."

events.ja: [[p:王賁]]は遼東に逃れた{n_yan}の王喜を捕らえ、燕を滅ぼした。
events.en: [[p:王賁|Wang Ben]] captured [[p:燕王喜|King Xi]] of {n_yan}, who had fled to Liaodong, and Yan was no more.

events.ja: 秦軍は戦わずして臨淄に入り、{n_qi}の[[p:王建]]は降った。
events.en: Qin's army entered Linzi without a fight, and [[p:王建|King Jian]] of {n_qi} surrendered.

events.ja: 天下は一つになった。{r_qin}は王の名では足りないとして「皇帝」を称し、自らを始皇帝とした。[[a:qin_unify|度量衡・文字・車軸の幅が統一され]]、天下は三十六郡に分けられた。
events.en: All under heaven was one. Finding "king" too small a word, {r_qin} took the title huangdi — emperor — and called himself the First Emperor. [[a:qin_unify|Weights, measures, script and axle widths were made one]], and the realm was divided into thirty-six commanderies.

deploy.ja: 晋は三軍に分かれた。中軍を[[p:先軫]]、上軍を狐毛と[[p:狐偃]]、下軍を欒枝と胥臣が率い、宋・斉・秦の兵が加わった。楚は子玉 ([[p:成得臣]]) が中軍に座し、左軍を子西、右軍を子上が率い、右軍の主力は従属する陳・蔡の兵であった。
deploy.en: Jin stood in three armies: [[p:先軫|Xian Zhen]] led the centre, Hu Mao and [[p:狐偃|Hu Yan]] the upper army, Luan Zhi and Xu Chen the lower, with troops of Song, Qi and Qin beside them. Ziyu ([[p:成得臣|Cheng Dechen]]) held the Chu centre, Zixi the left, Zishang the right — whose strength was the levies of the subject states Chen and Cai.

plan.ja: 晋の文公は、流浪の頃に楚の成王から受けた恩を返すとして「三舎」(九十里) を退いた。退いたことで晋は約束を守る者となり、楚は追う者となった。戦いが始まると、胥臣は馬に虎の皮をかぶせて陳・蔡の兵に突っ込み、楚の右軍はたちまち崩れた。欒枝は車の後ろに柴を引きずって土煙を上げ、敗走するように見せかけて楚の左軍を誘い出し、[[p:先軫]]と郤溱の中軍が横から突いた。中軍の子玉だけが兵を収めて退いた。
plan.en: Duke Wen of Jin fell back three days' march, to repay the kindness the King of Chu had shown him in his wandering years: Jin became the one who kept faith, Chu the one who pursued. When the fighting began, Xu Chen covered his horses with tiger skins and drove into the levies of Chen and Cai, and the Chu right collapsed. Luan Zhi dragged brushwood behind his chariots to raise dust, as if in flight, drew the Chu left out after him, and the centre under [[p:先軫|Xian Zhen]] struck it in the flank. Only Ziyu in the centre gathered his men and withdrew.

tales.ja: 戦いの前夜、文公は楚王と組み合って押し倒され、脳を吸われる夢を見て恐れた。[[p:狐偃]]は「天を仰いだ我らは天を得、地に伏した楚は罪に伏したのです」と解いて励ました。
tales.en: On the eve of battle Duke Wen dreamed the King of Chu wrestled him down and sucked his brains, and was afraid. [[p:狐偃|Hu Yan]] read it for him: "We lay facing heaven and have heaven; Chu bent over the earth, bowed down to its guilt."

tales.ja: 敗れた子玉は、楚王から「申と息の父老にどう顔向けするのか」と問われ、帰る途中で自ら命を絶った。それを聞いた文公は「これで私を害する者はいなくなった」と喜びを隠さなかったという。
tales.en: Beaten, Ziyu was asked by his king how he would face the elders of Shen and Xi, and took his own life on the way home. Hearing it, Duke Wen made no secret of his joy: "Now there is no one left to harm me."

after.ja: 戦いの後、晋は践土に王宮を築いて周の襄王を迎え、諸侯の盟を主宰した。王は文公を「侯伯」(諸侯の長) に任じ、晋はこの後百年近く中原の覇権を握る。
after.en: After the battle Jin built a palace at Jiantu, welcomed [[p:燕王喜|King Xi]]ang of Zhou there and presided over the covenant of the lords. The king named Duke Wen "elder of the lords", and Jin would hold the hegemony of the Central Plain for most of a century.

deploy.ja: 鄭を救いに来た晋の中軍は[[p:荀林父]]が率いたが、鄭が既に楚に降ったと知って帰るか戦うかで将たちが割れた。副将の[[p:先縠]]は勝手に兵を渡河させた。楚は荘王自ら陣頭に立った。
deploy.en: Jin had come to save Zheng, but when [[p:荀林父|Xun Linfu]], leading its centre, learned that Zheng had already gone over to Chu, his generals split over whether to fight or turn back; his deputy [[p:先縠|Xian Hu]] took troops across the river on his own.

plan.ja: 将が割れたまま戦いに引き込まれた晋軍に、楚軍は不意に押し寄せた。[[p:荀林父]]は「先に河を渡った者に賞を与える」と太鼓を打たせ、晋兵は舟に殺到した。上軍の[[p:士会]]だけが陣を崩さず退いた。
plan.en: With its generals divided Jin was drawn into battle, and the Chu army came on suddenly. [[p:荀林父|Xun Linfu]] beat the drums and promised a reward to the first back across the river; his men stampeded for the boats. Only [[p:士会|Shi Hui]] of the upper army withdrew in order.

tales.ja: 舟べりにすがる味方の指を斬り落として舟を出したため、舟の中の指は掬えるほどであったという。
tales.en: Men in the boats cut off the fingers of comrades clinging to the sides; the fingers in the bottoms, it is said, could be scooped up by the handful.

tales.ja: 楚兵は戦車の溝にはまって進めない晋兵に「横木を外せ」「旗を抜け」と教えてやった。晋兵は逃げながら「我らは大国 (楚) ほど逃げ慣れていない」と言い返した。
tales.en: Chu soldiers called out to Jin charioteers stuck in a rut how to pull out the crossbar and take down the flag; escaping, the men of Jin shouted back that they were not as practised at running as the great state of Chu.

tales.ja: 臣下が晋兵の屍を積んで「京観」(戦勝の塚) を築くよう勧めると、荘王は「武の字は戈を止めると書く」と退けた。
tales.en: When his ministers urged him to heap up the Jin dead into a victory mound, King Zhuang refused: the character for "martial", he said, is written "to stop the spear".

after.ja: 楚の荘王は覇者となり、鄭・宋も楚に従った。
after.en: King Zhuang of Chu became hegemon, and Zheng and Song followed Chu.

deploy.ja: 呉は精兵三万で、淮水をさかのぼった舟を捨て、一気に陸路で漢水へ出た。楚は令尹の[[p:囊瓦]] (子常) が二十万と号する大軍で漢水の西に陣した。
deploy.en: Wu came with thirty thousand picked men; it left its boats on the Huai and struck overland to the Han river. Chu's chief minister [[p:囊瓦|Nang Wa]] ([[p:子産|Zichan]]g) faced it west of the Han with a host said to number two hundred thousand.

plan.ja: 楚の[[p:沈尹戌]]は、自分が呉の舟を焼いて退路を断つ間、[[p:囊瓦]]に川を挟んで守るよう説いた。だが功を独り占めしたい[[p:囊瓦]]は川を渡って攻め、呉は三度戦って三度破った。柏挙では呉王の弟夫概が王の許しを待たず五千で突っ込み、楚軍を崩した。呉軍は五度戦って五度勝ち、郢に入った。
plan.en: [[p:沈尹戌|Shen Yin Xu]] of Chu proposed that [[p:囊瓦|Nang Wa]] hold the river while he burned the Wu boats behind them. [[p:囊瓦|Nang Wa]], wanting the glory for himself, crossed and attacked; Wu beat him three times. At Boju the king's brother Fugai charged with five thousand without waiting for leave and broke the Chu army. Fighting five battles and winning all five, Wu entered Ying.

tales.ja: [[p:孫武]]は呉王[[p:闔閭]]に兵法を説いたとき、宮中の女官百八十人を二隊に分けて調練し、笑って命に従わない隊長の寵姫二人を王の制止も聞かず斬った。以後、女官たちは一糸乱れず動いたという。
tales.en: When [[p:孫武|Sun Wu]] laid out the art of war for King [[p:闔閭|Helü]], he drilled a hundred and eighty palace women in two companies and, over the king's protests, beheaded the two favourites who led them for laughing at his orders. After that the women moved as one.

tales.ja: 郢に入った[[p:伍子胥]]は、父と兄を殺した平王の墓をあばいて屍に鞭打った。友の[[p:申包胥]]が「天理に背く」と責めると、「日暮れて道遠し、ゆえに倒行逆施す」と答えた。
tales.en: In Ying [[p:伍子胥|Wu Zixu]] dug up the body of King Ping, who had killed his father and brother, and flogged it. When his old friend [[p:申包胥|Shen Baoxu]] called it an outrage against heaven, he answered: "The day is late and the road is long; so I walk backwards and act against the grain."

after.ja: 楚の昭王は逃れ、[[p:申包胥]]の嘆願で秦の援軍が来ると、呉は郢を去った。この勝利で呉は南方の強国となった。
after.en: King Zhao of Chu fled; when [[p:申包胥|Shen Baoxu]] brought a Qin army with his pleading, Wu left Ying. The victory made Wu a great power of the south.

deploy.ja: 斉は[[p:田忌]]を将、[[p:孫臏]]を軍師として韓を救うため魏の都大梁を突いた。魏の[[p:龐涓]]は韓から兵を返し、太子申とともに斉軍を追った。
deploy.en: Qi sent [[p:田忌|Tian Ji]], with [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]] as his strategist, to strike at the Wei capital Daliang and so relieve Han. [[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]] of Wei pulled back from Han and, with the crown prince Shen, went after the Qi army.

plan.ja: [[p:孫臏]]は「魏の兵は斉を臆病と侮っている」と見て、初日は十万、翌日は五万、三日目は三万と、毎夜かまどの数を減らして見せた。[[p:龐涓]]は「斉兵は三日で半分以上逃げた」と喜び、歩兵を置いて騎兵だけで追った。[[p:孫臏]]は日暮れに着くと読んだ狭い馬陵の道に、一万の弩兵を伏せた。
plan.en: [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]] saw that Wei thought Qi's soldiers cowards. He had the army light a hundred thousand cooking fires the first night, fifty thousand the second, thirty thousand the third. "Half the men of Qi have deserted in three days!" [[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]] rejoiced, left his foot behind and pursued with the horse alone. [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]] hid ten thousand crossbowmen along the narrow road at Maling, where he reckoned [[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]] would arrive at dusk.

tales.ja: [[p:孫臏]]は大木の皮を削って「[[p:龐涓]]この樹の下に死す」と書かせ、「火が見えたら一斉に射よ」と命じた。夜、着いた[[p:龐涓]]が字を読もうと松明をともした瞬間、矢が降り注いだ。[[p:龐涓]]は「ついに豎子の名を成さしめたか」と言って自ら首を刎ねた。
tales.en: [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]] had the bark stripped from a great tree and wrote on it: "[[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]] dies beneath this tree", and told his archers to shoot as one when they saw a light. [[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]] arrived in the dark and lit a torch to read the words — and the arrows fell. "So I have made that wretch famous," he said, and cut his own throat.

tales.ja: かつて二人は同じ師に学んだ。[[p:孫臏]]の才を妬んだ[[p:龐涓]]は、[[p:孫臏]]を罪に陥れて両足を断つ刑に処し、顔に入れ墨をさせた。[[p:孫臏]]は斉の使者の車にひそかに隠れて魏を逃れていた。
tales.en: The two had studied under the same master. Jealous of [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]]'s gifts, [[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]] had him falsely accused, his feet cut off and his face tattooed; [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]] escaped Wei hidden in the carriage of a Qi envoy.

after.ja: 魏の太子申は捕らえられ、魏は戦国の初めの覇権を失った。斉の威王は東方の最強国となった。
after.en: The Wei crown prince Shen was captured and Wei lost the primacy it had held since the Warring States began. King Wei of Qi was master of the east.

deploy.ja: 上党を受け入れた趙に、秦は[[p:王齕]]の大軍を向けた。趙の老将[[p:廉頗]]は塁を固めて三年近く戦わず、秦の兵站を消耗させた。
deploy.en: Zhao accepted Shangdang, and Qin sent [[p:王齕|Wang He]] with a great army. The veteran [[p:廉頗|Lian Po]] built ramparts and would not fight for nearly three years, wearing down Qin's supply lines.

plan.ja: 秦の[[p:范雎]]は「秦が恐れるのは[[p:廉頗]]ではなく[[p:趙奢]]の子[[p:趙括]]だ」との噂を趙に流した。趙王は[[p:廉頗]]を退けて[[p:趙括]]を将とした。秦はひそかに[[p:白起]]を総大将に替え、偽って退いて[[p:趙括]]を塁の外へ誘い出し、二万五千の伏兵で退路を断ち、五千の騎兵で趙軍を二つに分けた。趙軍は四十六日間食を断たれ、互いに食らい合うほどになった。
plan.en: [[p:范雎|Fan Ju]] of Qin spread the word in Zhao that what Qin feared was not [[p:廉頗|Lian Po]] but [[p:趙括|Zhao Kuo]], son of [[p:趙奢|Zhao She]]. The King of Zhao replaced [[p:廉頗|Lian Po]] with [[p:趙括|Zhao Kuo]]. Qin secretly made [[p:白起|Bai Qi]] its commander, feigned a retreat to draw [[p:趙括|Zhao Kuo]] out of his ramparts, cut his line of retreat with twenty-five thousand men and split the Zhao army in two with five thousand horse. Without food for forty-six days, the Zhao soldiers were reduced to eating one another.

tales.ja: [[p:趙括]]は兵書をそらんじ、議論では父の[[p:趙奢]]も言い負かしたが、父は「戦は死地なのに、括は易々と口にする。趙を破るのは括だ」と言った。[[p:趙括]]の母も王に「あの子を将にしないでください」と願い出ていた。
tales.en: [[p:趙括|Zhao Kuo]] knew the books of war by heart and could outargue even his father, but [[p:趙奢|Zhao She]] said: "War is a place of death, and Kuo talks of it lightly; if Zhao is ever broken, it will be by him." His mother too begged the king not to make him general.

tales.ja: [[p:趙括]]は自ら突撃して射殺され、降った四十万の兵は、二百四十人の少年を除いて穴埋めにされたと伝わる。後に[[p:白起]]は「長平の降卒を欺いて殺した。わたしが死ぬのは当然だ」と言って自害した。
tales.en: [[p:趙括|Zhao Kuo]] led a last charge and was shot down. The four hundred thousand who surrendered were buried alive, the records say, all but two hundred and forty boys. Years later, ordered to die, [[p:白起|Bai Qi]] said: "I deceived and killed the men who surrendered at Changping. I deserve to die."

after.ja: 趙は国の力のほとんどを失い、秦は邯鄲を囲んだが、[[p:信陵君]]らの救援で退いた。それでも戦国の力の均衡はここで決定的に秦へ傾いた。
after.en: Zhao lost most of its strength. Qin besieged Handan, and was driven off by [[p:信陵君|Lord Xinling]] and others — but the balance of the Warring States had tipped to Qin for good.

name.en: Duke Huan of Qi's campaign against the Mountain Rong

terms.ja: 山戎は北へ退いた。燕の荘公が桓公を見送って斉の領内まで入ると、桓公は「諸侯を見送るのは国境まで」と、荘公が踏み入った土地を燕に与えた。
terms.en: The Mountain Rong fell back north. When Duke Zhuang of Yan, seeing Duke Huan off, crossed into Qi, Huan gave him the ground he had stood on: a lord sees another only to his own border.

terms.ja: 楚は宋の囲みを解いて退いた。晋は践土で周王を迎えて諸侯と盟を結び、文公は覇者となった。
terms.en: Chu lifted the siege of Song and withdrew. At Jiantu Jin received the king of Zhou and bound the lords in covenant; Duke Wen was hegemon.

terms.ja: 晋は河の北へ退き、鄭は楚に従った。
terms.en: Jin fell back north of the river and Zheng followed Chu.

terms.ja: [[p:申包胥]]が秦の庭で七日七晩泣き続けて得た秦の援軍が来ると、呉は郢を去った。
terms.en: When the army of Qin came — won by [[p:申包胥|Shen Baoxu]], who wept seven days and nights in the Qin court — Wu left Ying.

terms.ja: 姑蘇は三年の囲みの末に落ち、呉王[[p:夫差]]は「子胥に合わせる顔がない」と顔を布で覆って自害した。呉は越に併せられた。
terms.en: Gusu fell after a three-year siege. King [[p:夫差|Fuchai]] of Wu covered his face — "I cannot face [[p:伍子胥|Wu Zixu]]" — and killed himself; Wu was joined to Yue.

terms.ja: 魏は太子申と[[p:龐涓]]を失い、斉に和を請うた。
terms.en: Wei, having lost the crown prince Shen and [[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]], sued Qi for peace.

name.ja: 子之の乱と斉の燕侵攻
name.en: the troubles of Zizhi and Qi's invasion of Yan

terms.ja: 諸侯の非難と燕人の抵抗に、斉軍は燕から引き揚げた。燕は昭王を立て、後に[[p:楽毅]]を用いて斉に報いる。
terms.en: Under the censure of the lords and the resistance of the people of Yan, Qi withdrew. Yan enthroned King Zhao, who would later repay Qi through [[p:楽毅|Yue Yi]].

terms.ja: 長平の後、秦は邯鄲を囲んだが、魏の[[p:信陵君]]と楚の[[p:春申君]]の救援に破れて退いた。趙は持ちこたえたが、国力は戻らなかった。
terms.en: After Changping Qin besieged Handan, but was beaten off by the relief armies of [[p:信陵君|Lord Xinling]] of Wei and [[p:春申君|Lord Chunshen]] of Chu. Zhao survived, but never recovered its strength.

body.ja:
前307年、趙の[[p:武霊王]]は「胡服騎射」を命じた。胡服とは北方の遊牧の民の服である。筒袖の短い上着、馬にまたがれるズボン (袴)、革の長靴、帯を留める金具。中原の貴族は裾の長い衣を着て、戦では戦車の上に立って戦っていた。裾を引きずる衣では馬に乗れない。王は、服から変えなければ騎兵は生まれないと考えた。

反対は激しかった。服は礼であり、礼こそが中華と夷狄を分けるもの、というのが貴族たちの考えであった。王の叔父の公子成は病と称して朝廷に出てこなかった。王は自ら叔父の屋敷を訪ね、「服は着る者の便のため、礼は事を成すためのものです。聖人は国を利するなら古いしきたりにこだわりません」と説いた。翌日、公子成は胡服を着て朝廷に現れた。

なぜ騎兵だったのか。趙は北と西で林胡・楼煩などの遊牧の民と境を接していた。彼らは馬上から弓を射て、戦車の入れない山や草原を自在に駆け回る。戦車は平らな土地でしか使えず、一台に馬四頭と兵三人が要る。騎兵なら一頭に一人、山でも谷でも行ける。[[p:武霊王]]は、敵の戦い方そのものを取り入れたのである。

効き目はすぐに現れた。趙は林胡・楼煩を討って雲中・雁門・代の郡を置き、長年の敵であった中山国を滅ぼした。降った楼煩の騎兵も自軍に組み入れ、趙の北辺の騎兵は戦国で最も強いと言われるようになった。のちに匈奴の大軍を破った名将[[p:李牧]]も、この騎兵を率いて戦っている。

王の最期は悲劇であった。王は位を若い子 ([[p:恵文王]]) に譲って自らは「主父」と名乗り、なお軍を率い続けた。ところが、廃した長子の反乱に巻き込まれ、沙丘の離宮を三か月余り囲まれて、雀の雛まで食べ尽くして餓死したという。

胡服の影響は戦場の外にも残った。ズボンと長靴、帯の留め金 (帯鉤) はやがて中国の兵の普通の装いとなり、騎兵は秦と漢の軍の柱となっていく。「胡服騎射」は、伝統より実利を選んだ改革の代名詞として、今も語られている。
body.en:
In 307 BC [[p:武霊王|King Wuling]] of Zhao ordered "barbarian dress and mounted archery". The "barbarian dress" was the clothing of the northern herders: a short jacket with narrow sleeves, trousers a man could sit a horse in, leather boots and a belt hook. The nobles of the Central Plain wore long robes and fought standing in chariots — and no one can ride in a robe that trails on the ground. Without a change of clothes, the king reasoned, there would be no cavalry.

The opposition was fierce. Dress was ritual, said the nobles, and ritual was what set the civilised apart from the barbarians. The king's uncle, Prince Cheng, pleaded illness and stayed away from court. The king went to his house himself: "Clothes are for the convenience of those who wear them; rites are for getting things done. A sage does not cling to old custom when the state can gain by changing it." The next day Prince Cheng came to court in trousers.

Why horsemen? To the north and west Zhao bordered herding peoples such as the Linhu and the Loufan, who shot from horseback and ranged over mountains and grassland where no chariot could go. A chariot needs flat ground, four horses and three men; a horseman needs one horse and goes anywhere. [[p:武霊王|King Wuling]] simply took over his enemies' way of fighting.

It worked at once. Zhao struck the Linhu and Loufan, set up the commanderies of Yunzhong, Yanmen and Dai, and destroyed its old enemy, the state of Zhongshan. The Loufan horsemen who surrendered were taken into the army, and the cavalry of Zhao's northern frontier came to be thought the best of the Warring States. [[p:李牧|Li Mu]], who later crushed a great Xiongnu army, led these horsemen.

The king's end was tragic. He handed the throne to a young son ([[p:恵文王|King Huiwen]]), styled himself "the Lord Father" and went on leading armies — until he was caught up in the revolt of the elder son he had set aside, besieged in the palace at Shaqiu for more than three months, and starved to death after eating even the sparrow chicks in the eaves.

The change outlived him. Trousers, boots and belt hooks became the ordinary wear of Chinese soldiers, and cavalry became a pillar of the armies of Qin and Han. "Barbarian dress and mounted archery" is still the byword for a reform that put use before tradition.

title.en: The chariots of the Spring and Autumn

body.ja:
春秋の戦いの主役は、二頭または四頭の馬が引く二輪の戦車であった。車の上には三人が乗る。左に弓を持つ車左、右に戈 (ほこ) を持つ車右、中央で手綱を取る御者。車の後ろには数十人の歩兵が従い、戦車一台とその歩兵が一つの単位となった。

国の力は戦車の数で数えられた。「千乗の国」「万乗の君」という言葉は、戦車を千台、一万台出せる国、という意味である。城濮の戦いで晋が出した戦車は七百乗であった。

戦車の戦いには礼があった。整列を待たずに攻めない、逃げる敵を深追いしない、傷ついた者を重ねて傷つけない。泓水の戦い (前638年) で、宋の襄公は楚軍が河を渡りきり陣を整えるまで攻撃を待ち、大敗して自らも腿に傷を負い、翌年死んだ。後世「宋襄の仁」として笑われる話である。邲の戦いでは、楚兵が溝にはまった晋の戦車に抜け出し方を教えてやったという。

戦車は平地でしか力を出せない。山がちな北の地で狄と戦った晋の軍では、前541年、魏舒の進言で兵を車から降ろして歩兵の隊列を組ませ (「車を毀ちて行と為す」)、大原で狄を破った。戦国時代になると、歩兵の大軍と騎兵、そして弩が戦場を支配し、戦車はしだいに指揮官の乗り物となっていく。

戦車と弓の術は国から国へ伝わった。楚から晋へ亡命した巫臣は、晋の命で南の呉に渡り、戦車の御し方と陣の組み方を教えた。それまで舟と歩兵で戦っていた呉はこうして中原の戦い方を身につけ、八十年ほど後には楚の都に攻め入ることになる。
body.en:
The decisive arm of Spring and Autumn warfare was the two-wheeled chariot drawn by two or four horses. Three men rode in it: an archer on the left, a man with a dagger-axe on the right, and the driver in the middle. Behind came a few dozen foot soldiers; a chariot and its men made one unit.

A state's power was counted in chariots. "A state of a thousand chariots", "a lord of ten thousand chariots" meant one that could field that many. At Chengpu, Jin put seven hundred chariots in the field.

Chariot warfare had its courtesies: no attack before the enemy had formed up, no long pursuit of the fleeing, no second wound to the wounded. At the Hong river in 638 BC Duke Xiang of Song waited for the Chu army to cross and form its lines before attacking; he was routed, took a wound in the thigh and died the next year — "the benevolence of Duke Xiang" became a byword for folly. At Bi, Chu soldiers showed Jin charioteers stuck in a ditch how to get out.

Chariots need flat ground. Fighting the Di in the hills of the north in 541 BC, a Jin army on Wei Shu's advice broke up its chariots and formed its men into infantry files, and won at Dayuan. By the Warring States, masses of infantry, cavalry and the crossbow ruled the battlefield, and the chariot became a commander's vehicle.

The art of chariot and bow passed from state to state. Wuchen, an exile from Chu in Jin, was sent south to Wu to teach it how to drive chariots and draw up battle lines. Wu, which had fought with boats and foot soldiers, learned the ways of the Central Plain — and some eighty years later stormed the capital of Chu.

body.ja:
弩は、引き絞った弦を引き金の仕掛け (懸刀) で留めておき、狙いを定めてから放つ弓である。弓のように腕の力で引いたまま狙う必要がないので、力の弱い兵でも短い訓練で使え、強い弓よりも遠くへ、鎧を貫くほどの力で射ることができた。

戦国時代、弩は歩兵の主な武器となった。「天下の強い弓と弩はみな韓から出る」と言われ、韓の弩は六百歩先まで届いたという (遊説家[[p:蘇秦]]の言葉として伝わる)。青銅で精密に鋳た引き金の部品は形がそろい、壊れても取り替えることができた。

馬陵の戦いで[[p:孫臏]]は一万の弩兵を道の両側に伏せ、[[p:龐涓]]の軍を一斉の射撃で崩した。弩は隊列で一斉に放つときに最も力を発揮する。前の列が撃つ間に後ろの列が弦を張る、交代で撃つ工夫もされた。

始皇帝陵の兵馬俑には、ひざまずいて弩を構える兵の像が並んでいる。漢の時代には、足で弦を踏んで引く強い弩 (蹶張) が、北の騎兵に対する切り札となった。

西方にも古代ギリシアの「腹当て弓」のような弩はあったが、広く使われたのは中世になってからである。東アジアでは二千年以上前に、すでに弩が大量に作られ、組織的に使われていた。
body.en:
A crossbow holds the drawn string on a trigger catch until the archer has taken aim. Since nobody has to hold the draw with the strength of his arms, weaker men could learn it quickly, and it shot farther and harder than a strong bow — hard enough to pierce armour.

In the Warring States the crossbow became the infantry's main weapon. "All the strong bows and crossbows under heaven come from Han," it was said, and the crossbows of Han reached six hundred paces — so the persuader [[p:蘇秦|Su Qin]] is supposed to have told its king. The bronze trigger parts were cast so precisely that they matched and could be swapped when broken.

At Maling [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]] hid ten thousand crossbowmen on both sides of the road and broke [[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]]'s army with a single volley. Crossbows are at their best shot together in ranks; men learned to take turns, the rear rank spanning while the front rank shot.

Among the terracotta warriors of the First Emperor's tomb kneel crossbowmen ready to shoot. Under the Han, powerful crossbows spanned with the feet became the trump card against the horsemen of the north.

The West had crossbows too — the "belly bow" of ancient Greece — but they spread widely only in the Middle Ages. In East Asia they were made in great numbers and used in organised ranks more than two thousand years ago.

body.ja:
戦国の初め、魏の文侯は[[p:呉起]]に命じて精兵「武卒」を選ばせた。[[p:荀子]]によれば、その試験は、三重の鎧を着て、十二石の弩を引き、矢五十本を背負い、戈をかつぎ、兜をかぶり剣を帯び、三日分の食糧を担いで、半日で百里を走ること。合格すれば家の税と労役を免じられ、田と家を与えられた。

[[p:呉起]]は兵と同じものを食べ、同じ所に寝て、馬にも乗らず、自分の食糧は自分で担いだ。兵の腫れ物の膿を口で吸い出してやったとき、その兵の母は声を上げて泣いた。「あの子の父も将軍に膿を吸っていただき、ご恩に報いようと退かずに戦って死にました。あの子もきっと同じことになるでしょう」。

武卒を率いた[[p:呉起]]は秦から河西の地を奪い、諸侯と七十六度戦って六十四度勝ち、残りも引き分けたという。魏は戦国の初めの最強国となった。

しかし[[p:荀子]]は武卒の弱点も指摘している。一度選ばれると、年を取って衰えても特権は取り上げられない。新しく選ぶにも費用がかかる。国が豊かでも兵の数を増やせない。呉起が魏を去り、馬陵で魏が敗れたのち、選ばれた精兵の時代は、秦の軍功爵による大動員の時代に取って代わられていった。
body.en:
At the start of the Warring States Marquis Wen of Wei had [[p:呉起|Wu Qi]] select an elite infantry, the "martial soldiers". [[p:荀子|Xunzi]] describes the test: in three layers of armour, spanning a twelve-stone crossbow, with fifty arrows on the back, a dagger-axe on the shoulder, helmet and sword, and three days' food, a man had to cover a hundred li by noon. Those who passed were freed from tax and labour and given fields and a house.

[[p:呉起|Wu Qi]] ate what his men ate, slept where they slept, would not ride, and carried his own food. When he sucked the pus from a soldier's abscess, the soldier's mother wailed: "The general did the same for his father, who would not turn back in battle to repay him, and died. Now my son will too."

Leading these soldiers [[p:呉起|Wu Qi]] took the land west of the Yellow River from Qin and fought the lords seventy-six times, winning sixty-four and drawing the rest, it is said. Wei became the first great power of the Warring States.

[[p:荀子|Xunzi]] also saw the weakness. A man once chosen kept his privileges even when he grew old and weak; choosing new men was costly; a rich state still could not field more of them. After Wu Qi left Wei and Wei was beaten at Maling, the age of picked soldiers gave way to the mass levies of Qin and its ranks for heads.

body.ja:
[[p:商鞅]]の変法で、秦は爵位を戦の手柄で与えることにした。敵の甲冑の兵の首を一つ取れば、爵一級と田一頃・宅地九畝、それに召し使う者一人。爵は二十の等級に分かれ、上がるほど田と税の免除が増え、罪を爵で償うこともできた。

反対に、王の一族でも軍功がなければ一族の籍から外された。家柄ではなく首の数が身分を決める——中原の諸侯から見れば野蛮だったが、秦の農民には出世の道が開かれた。秦の兵は戦場で兜を脱ぎ捨て、左手に敵の首を下げ、右脇に捕虜を抱えて駆けた、と遊説家の[[p:張儀]]は語っている。

五家を一組とする「伍」の仕組みもあった。一人が罪を犯せば組の皆が罰せられ、互いに見張り合う。農と戦のほかに出世の道はふさがれ、国全体が兵と兵糧を生み出す仕組みとなった。

この仕組みが長平の戦いのような大動員を可能にした。長平では、秦王が自ら河内に出向いて民に爵を一級ずつ与え、十五歳以上の男子をすべて送り込んだと伝わる。秦の統一は、この冷徹な仕組みの上に築かれた。
body.en:
Under [[p:商鞅|Shang Yang]]'s reforms Qin gave rank for deeds in war. One head of an armoured enemy soldier earned one degree of rank, a hundred mu of land, nine mu for a house and a servant. There were twenty degrees; the higher a man rose, the more land and freedom from tax he had, and rank could buy off punishment.

The other way round, members of the royal clan with no merit in war were struck from its register. Heads, not birth, made a man's place — barbarous in the eyes of the Central Plain, but a road upward for Qin's farmers. The soldiers of Qin, said the persuader [[p:張儀|Zhang Yi]], threw off their helmets and ran at the enemy with a head in the left hand and a prisoner under the right arm.

Households were grouped in fives: if one broke the law, all were punished, so all watched each other. Every road to advancement but farming and war was closed, and the whole state became a machine for soldiers and grain.

That machine made levies like Changping possible: the king, it is said, went himself to Henei, gave every man a degree of rank and sent every male over fifteen to the front. The unification of China was built on it.

title.en: The swords of Wu and Yue

body.ja:
春秋の終わり、長江の下流の呉と越は、名剣の国として知られた。青銅に錫を合わせる割合を変えて、刃は硬く、芯は粘り強く鋳分ける技があったという。

伝説の刀工も多い。越の欧冶子は越王のために「湛盧」「純鈞」など五振りの剣を鍛えた。呉王[[p:闔閭]]に命じられた干将は、炉の鉄がどうしても溶けず、妻の莫耶が髪と爪を炉に投じてようやく溶けたという。こうして鍛えた雌雄二振りの剣が「干将」と「莫耶」である。

1965年、湖北省の楚の墓から一振りの剣が掘り出された。刃には鳥の形をした文字で「越王鳩浅 (勾践) 自ら作りて用いる剣」とある。二千四百年以上土の中にあったのに錆はほとんどなく、刃は紙を何枚も重ねて切れたという。越の剣がなぜ楚の墓に入ったのか——嫁入り道具だったのか、戦利品だったのか——は分かっていない。

剣にまつわる美しい話もある。呉の公子[[p:季札]]が北へ使いに行く途中、徐の君主が[[p:季札]]の剣を欲しそうに見ていた。使いの途中なので贈れなかった季札が帰りに立ち寄ると、徐君はもう亡くなっていた。季札は剣を外して墓の木に掛けて去った。「心の中で贈ると決めていたのだから、相手が死んだからといって約束を破れようか」。
body.en:
At the end of the Spring and Autumn the lower Yangzi states of Wu and Yue were famous for their swords. Their smiths cast blades in which the proportion of tin to copper differed — a hard edge, a tougher core.

Legendary smiths abound. Ou Yezi forged five swords for the king of Yue, among them Zhanlu and Chunjun. Gan Jiang, set to work by King [[p:闔閭|Helü]] of Wu, could not get his iron to melt until his wife Mo Ye threw her hair and nail clippings into the furnace; the pair of swords that came of it bear their names.

In 1965 a sword was dug from a Chu tomb in Hubei. Its blade carries, in bird-shaped script, "[[p:句践|Goujian]], King of Yue, made this sword for his own use". After more than 2,400 years underground it was barely tarnished, and could still cut through a stack of paper. How a Yue sword came to lie in a Chu grave — dowry or booty — no one knows.

There is a gentle story too. [[p:季札|Ji Zha]], a prince of Wu travelling north as envoy, saw that the lord of Xu admired his sword. An envoy cannot give away his sword mid-journey; when [[p:季札|Ji Zha]] came back, the lord of Xu was dead. He hung the sword on a tree by the grave and went on. "I had promised it in my heart. Should his death make me break my word?"

title.en: The fish and salt of Qi

body.ja:
周の初め、太公望 (呂尚) が封じられた斉の地は、海辺の痩せた塩の土地で、人も少なかった。太公望は女たちの手仕事 (織物) を勧め、魚と塩の利を通わせた。すると人も物も四方から集まり、斉は大国となった、と『史記』は書く。

斉の桓公を覇者にした宰相[[p:管仲]]は、塩を国の財源にした。海水を煮て塩を作らせ、国がそれを買い上げて他国へ高く売る。塩は誰もが毎日なめる。税を重くしなくても、塩の値で国庫は満ちる——後の時代まで続く「塩の専売」の始まりと言われる。

都の臨淄は戦国時代、七万戸を数える大都市となった。遊説家の[[p:蘇秦]]は、道を行く車の車輪がぶつかり合い、人の肩がこすれ合い、袖を連ねれば幕となり、汗を払えば雨となる、と賑わいを語っている。人々は竽 (笛) を吹き、琴を弾き、闘鶏や犬の競走、蹴鞠に興じた。
body.en:
When the Grand Duke Lü Shang was given Qi at the start of the Zhou, it was poor, salty, sparsely peopled land by the sea. He encouraged the women's crafts and the trade in fish and salt, says the Records of the Grand Historian, and people and goods came from every side until Qi was a great state.

[[p:管仲|Guan Zhong]], the minister who made Duke Huan of Qi hegemon, made salt the treasury's mainstay: brine was boiled down, the state bought the salt and sold it dear abroad. Everyone eats salt every day; with no heavier taxes the treasury filled — the beginning, it is said, of the salt monopoly that later dynasties kept.

By the Warring States the capital Linzi had seventy thousand households. Its streets, said the persuader [[p:蘇秦|Su Qin]], were so crowded that chariot hubs knocked and shoulders rubbed; raised sleeves made a curtain and wiped sweat fell like rain. Its people played pipes and zithers and amused themselves with cockfights, dog races and football.

title.en: The silks of Qi and Lu

body.ja:
斉の「紈」は白く薄い練り絹、魯の「縞」は薄く細かい生絹。どちらも天下に名高く、「斉は冠・帯・衣・履で天下を覆う」と言われるほど、斉の衣服は諸国に行き渡った。

絹は戦にも使われた。『管子』には、斉の桓公が[[p:管仲]]の策で、わざと隣の魯と梁の厚絹 (綈) の服を着て国中に流行らせた話がある。魯と梁の民は畑を捨てて機を織った。頃合いを見て斉が買うのをやめると、二国は食糧が尽き、斉に従うしかなくなった。経済で国を降した話として語られる。

魯の縞の薄さは、のちの言い回しにも残った。「強い弩の矢も、飛び尽くしたところでは魯の縞さえ貫けない」(強弩の末、魯縞を穿つ能わず)。どれほど強い力も、勢いが尽きれば何もできない、という意味である。
body.en:
The wan of Qi was a fine white glossed silk, the gao of Lu a thin, close raw silk; both were famous, and Qi, it was said, "capped, belted, clothed and shod the whole world".

Silk could be a weapon. The Guanzi tells how Duke Huan of Qi, on [[p:管仲|Guan Zhong]]'s advice, made a fashion of wearing the heavy silk of his neighbours Lu and Liang. Their people left the fields to weave. When the moment came Qi stopped buying, and the two states, out of grain, had to bow to Qi — a conquest by trade.

The thinness of Lu silk entered a proverb: "An arrow from the strongest crossbow, at the end of its flight, cannot pierce the silk of Lu" — even the greatest force can do nothing once its momentum is spent.

body.ja:
南の大国楚の墓からは、赤と黒の漆を塗り重ねた器や道具が数多く出てくる。酒を飲む耳杯、化粧箱、太鼓の台、そして角を生やして舌を垂らした不思議な「鎮墓獣」。湿った土の中でも木を守る漆のおかげで、二千年以上たっても色は鮮やかなままである。

漆の木から採った樹液を薄く何十回も塗り重ね、乾かしては磨く。手間のかかる品で、漢の頃の記録では、一つの漆の杯は銅の杯の十倍の値がしたという。

思想家の[[p:荘子]]は、若い頃、宋の蒙という町で「漆園の吏」(漆畑の役人) を務めていた。楚の王が宰相に迎えようとしたとき、[[p:荘子]]は「死んで廟に祭られる亀より、生きて泥の中で尾を引きずっていたい」と言って断ったという。
body.en:
The tombs of the great southern state of Chu are full of objects coated in layer upon layer of red and black lacquer: ear-handled wine cups, cosmetic boxes, drum stands, and the strange antlered "tomb guardians" with lolling tongues. Lacquer protects wood even in wet earth, and their colours are bright after more than two thousand years.

Sap from the lacquer tree is laid on thinly dozens of times, dried and polished each time. It was costly work; in Han times a lacquered cup was worth ten bronze ones, the records say.

The philosopher [[p:荘子|Zhuangzi]] was, as a young man, an officer of the lacquer gardens at Meng in Song. When the King of Chu offered to make him chief minister he declined: better to be a live turtle dragging its tail in the mud than a dead one honoured in a temple.

body.ja:
中国の鉄は、西方と違ってまず「鋳鉄」として広まった。高温の炉で鉄を溶かし、型に流して作る。青銅を鋳る技の長い伝統があったからだと考えられている。

前513年、晋の趙鞅らは鉄で鼎を鋳て、そこに刑法を刻んだ (刑鼎)。鉄の確かな記録の中でも早いものである。[[p:孔子]]は「民が鼎を見て法を知れば、貴人を尊ばなくなる」と嘆いたという。

楚の宛は鉄の名産地で、「宛の鉅鉄の矛は蜂やさそりのように鋭い」と[[p:荀子]]は書いている。戦国時代には鉄の鋤や鍬が農民に行き渡り、荒れ地が耕され、人が増えた。鉄の斧で森が開かれ、深く掘れる鍬で水路が引かれた。

鉄は大金持ちも生んだ。趙の邯鄲で鉄を商った郭縦は王侯と並ぶ富を持ち、同じく趙の鉄商人卓氏は、秦に国を滅ぼされて蜀へ移されると、臨邛の鉄山で再び財を成し、千人の召し使いを抱えたと『史記』は伝える。
body.en:
Iron in China spread first as cast iron, unlike in the West: melted in hot furnaces and poured into moulds — thanks, it is thought, to the long tradition of casting bronze.

In 513 BC Zhao Yang of Jin and others cast an iron cauldron and inscribed the laws on it, one of the earliest sure records of iron. [[p:孔子|Confucius]] lamented that once the people could read the law on a cauldron, they would no longer honour the nobles.

Wan in Chu was famous for iron: "the iron spears of Wan are as sharp as wasps and scorpions," [[p:荀子|Xunzi]] wrote. By the Warring States iron ploughshares and hoes were in every farmer's hands; wasteland was broken, forests cleared with iron axes, canals dug with deep hoes, and people multiplied.

Iron made fortunes too. Guo Zong, an iron dealer of Handan, was as rich as a king; the Zhuo family, iron merchants of Zhao deported to Shu when Qin destroyed their state, made a second fortune from the iron hills of Linqiong and kept a thousand servants, says the Records of the Grand Historian.

body.ja:
斉の桓公は、かつて自分に矢を射かけた[[p:管仲]]を、親友の[[p:鮑叔牙]]に勧められて宰相に迎えた。管仲は斉を、春秋で最初の覇者の国に作り変えた。

管仲はまず民を四つに分けて住まわせた。士 (武士)・農・工・商。同じ仕事の者が集まって住めば、子は親の技を見て自然に覚え、余計な望みを持たない、と考えたのである。さらに村の組織をそのまま軍の組織とし (内政に軍令を寄せる)、五家が一組の伍は戦では五人の伍となった。幼い頃から共に暮らした者同士は、夜の戦でも声で互いを知り、死を共にできる。

国の財は海から得た。海水を煮て塩を作り、鉄を管理し、物の値の上下を見て国が買い入れ売り払う。管仲の言葉として「倉が満ちて礼節を知り、衣食が足りて栄誉と恥を知る」が伝わる。

桓公はこの力で諸侯を集め、周の王を尊び、北の山戎や南の楚を討った。[[p:孔子]]はのちに「管仲がいなければ、私たちは今ごろ髪を振り乱し、着物を左前に着ていただろう (夷狄の風になっていただろう)」と言った。
body.en:
Duke Huan of Qi made [[p:管仲|Guan Zhong]] his chief minister — the man who had once shot an arrow at him — on the word of Guan Zhong's friend [[p:鮑叔牙|Bao Shuya]]. Guan Zhong made Qi the first hegemon of the Spring and Autumn.

He began by settling the people in four orders, each in its own quarter: officers, farmers, craftsmen and merchants. Living among their own trade, children learned it from their parents and wanted nothing else. He made the village the army, too: five households were five men in a file, and men who had grown up together knew each other's voices in a night battle and would die for one another.

Wealth came from the sea: brine boiled into salt, iron under the state's hand, and the state buying cheap and selling dear as prices rose and fell. A saying is put in his mouth: "When the granaries are full, people know propriety; when food and clothing suffice, they know honour and shame."

With this strength Duke Huan gathered the lords, honoured the king of Zhou and struck the Mountain Rong in the north and Chu in the south. "But for Guan Zhong," [[p:孔子|Confucius]] said, "we should all be wearing our hair loose and folding our robes to the left like barbarians."

body.ja:
周の昔の田は「井田」であった、と後の書物は言う。九つに区切った田のうち、まわりの八区画を八家がそれぞれ耕し、真ん中の一区画を皆で耕して、その収穫を領主に納める。

前594年、魯は初めて、田の広さに応じて一律に税を取った (初税畝)。共同で耕す田の収穫ではなく、それぞれの田から税を取る——言いかえれば、民が自分で切り開いた田も、その者の田として認めたことになる。『左伝』は「礼にかなっていない」と書いたが、流れは止まらなかった。

鄭の[[p:子産]]は前538年に「丘賦」(土地に応じた軍の負担) を定め、秦も前408年に「初めて禾 (穀物) を租とした」。土地に税をかける仕組みは、戦国の国々が民を直接治め、兵と食糧を集める土台となっていく。
body.en:
In the old days of Zhou, later books say, the fields were "well fields": a square of nine plots, eight farmed by eight families for themselves and the middle one farmed by all for the lord.

In 594 BC Lu for the first time taxed every field by its area. Not the harvest of the common plot but a share of each field — in effect, the land a family had broken for itself became its own. The Zuo Commentary called it "not according to the rites", but the tide did not turn back.

[[p:子産|Zichan]] of Zheng set a military levy by land in 538 BC, and Qin "first took grain as tax" in 408 BC. Taxing the land became the footing on which the Warring States ruled their people directly and raised soldiers and food.

title.ja: 法を民に示す (刑書と刑鼎)

body.ja:
それまで刑罰の決まりは、貴族たちが胸に秘めて、その時々に裁くものであった。前536年、鄭の宰相[[p:子産]]は、刑法を青銅の鼎に鋳込んで人々に示した (刑書)。

晋の賢人[[p:叔向]]は子産に手紙を送って責めた。「民が法を知れば、上を恐れず、条文を盾に争うようになる。国は滅びるだろう」。子産は短く答えた。「私には子孫のことまで考える才はない。ただ世を救うためにするのだ」。

前513年には晋も、趙鞅らが鉄の鼎に刑法を鋳込んだ。[[p:孔子]]は「民が鼎を見て法を知れば、貴人を尊ぶだろうか」と嘆いたという。

鄭ではさらに、鄧析という人が竹簡に法を書き写した「竹刑」を作り、人々の訴えを手伝った。鄧析は前501年に処刑されたが、その竹刑は使われ続けた。法を誰もが読めるものにする流れは、戦国の法家へとつながっていく。
body.en:
Until then the rules of punishment were kept in the nobles' heads and applied as they saw fit. In 536 BC [[p:子産|Zichan]], chief minister of Zheng, cast the laws on bronze cauldrons for all to see.

[[p:叔向|Shuxiang]], the wise man of Jin, wrote to rebuke him: "When the people know the law they will not fear their betters; they will quarrel over its words, and the state will perish." Zichan replied briefly: "I lack the talent to think of my descendants. I do it to save the present age."

In 513 BC Jin too, under Zhao Yang, cast its laws on an iron cauldron. [[p:孔子|Confucius]] lamented: once the people read the law on the cauldron, would they still honour the noble?

In Zheng a man named Deng Xi copied the laws onto bamboo — the "bamboo code" — and helped people with their suits. He was put to death in 501 BC, but his code stayed in use. Making the law something anyone could read led on to the Legalists of the Warring States.

body.ja:
戦国の初め、魏の文侯は[[p:李悝]]を用いて国を立て直した。李悝は「土地の力を尽くす教え」を説いた。同じ広さの田でも、よく耕せば収穫は大きく増える。勤めれば増え、怠ければ減る——それが国全体では大きな差になる。

李悝はまた「平糴法」を定めた。豊作の年には国が穀物を買い上げて値崩れを防ぎ、不作の年には蓄えを売り出して値上がりを抑える。農民も町の民も守られ、魏は豊かになった。

李悝がまとめた『法経』六篇 (盗・賊・囚・捕・雑・具) は、中国の法典の始まりとされる。[[p:商鞅]]はこれを秦に持って行き、秦の法の土台とした。「食は労ある者に、禄は功ある者に」——家柄ではなく働きで報いるという考えも、李悝のものとして伝わる。
body.en:
At the start of the Warring States Marquis Wen of Wei rebuilt his state with [[p:李悝|Li Kui]]. Li Kui taught "making the most of the land": the same field gives far more if worked well, and the difference, across a whole country, is enormous.

He also set up the "even purchase" law: in good years the state bought grain so the price would not collapse, in bad years it sold from its stores to keep the price down. Farmers and townsfolk were both protected, and Wei grew rich.

His Canon of Laws in six books — theft, violence, prisons, arrest, miscellany and general rules — is counted the first Chinese code. [[p:商鞅|Shang Yang]] took it to Qin, where it became the base of Qin law. "Food to those who labour, stipends to those of merit" — reward by deeds rather than birth — is also attributed to him.

body.ja:
魏を追われた名将[[p:呉起]]は、南の楚の悼王に迎えられて令尹 (宰相) となった。呉起は、楚が大きいのに弱いのは、貴族が多すぎるからだと見た。

呉起は、三代を過ぎた貴族の封地と俸禄を取り上げ、貴族たちを人の少ない辺境の地に移し、役に立たない役人を減らした。浮いた財で兵を養い、楚は南の百越を従え、北では陳・蔡を併せ、三晋を退けた。

だが恨みは深かった。前381年、悼王が死ぬと、貴族たちは葬儀の場で呉起に矢を射かけた。呉起は王の亡骸に覆いかぶさって死んだ。王の遺体に矢を当てるのは大罪である。新しい王は、王の亡骸を射た者を罪に問い、七十余りの家が滅ぼされた。呉起は死んでなお、仇に報いたのである。
body.en:
Driven from Wei, the great general [[p:呉起|Wu Qi]] was welcomed by King Dao of Chu and made chief minister. Chu, he saw, was big but weak because it carried too many nobles.

He took back the fiefs and stipends of noble lines three generations old, moved the nobles to empty frontier lands and cut useless offices. The savings fed soldiers; Chu subdued the Hundred Yue in the south, swallowed Chen and Cai in the north and drove back the three Jin states.

The hatred ran deep. When King Dao died in 381 BC the nobles shot at Wu Qi during the funeral. He threw himself over the king's body and died there. To strike a king's corpse was a great crime: the new king punished all who had shot at it, and more than seventy families were wiped out. Even in death Wu Qi repaid his enemies.

body.ja:
衛の公子に生まれた[[p:商鞅]] (衛鞅) は、魏で用いられず、西の秦の孝公に仕えた。前356年と前350年の二度の変法で、商鞅は秦を戦国最強の国に作り変えた。

まず民を五家・十家の組に分け、一人の罪を組の皆の罪とした。戦で首を取った者には爵を与え ([[a:qin_rank|軍功爵]])、王族でも功がなければ一族の籍から外した。成人の男子が二人以上いる家には税を倍にして、家を分けさせた。都を咸陽に移し、小さな村々をまとめて四十一の県とし、県令を置いて王が直接治めた。田のあぜを改め、升や秤の大きさを国中でそろえた。そのとき作られた青銅の升 (商鞅方升) が今も残っている。

法を信じさせるため、商鞅は都の南門に三丈の木を立て、「北門に移した者に十金を与える」と告げた。誰も信じないので五十金に上げると、ある男が移し、本当に五十金をもらった。

前338年、孝公が死ぬと、恨みを買っていた商鞅は追われる身となった。逃げて宿を求めると、宿の主人は「商君の法で、旅の証のない客を泊めると罰せられます」と断った。商鞅は「法を作った者が、その法に苦しむとは」と嘆いたという。商鞅は捕らえられ、車裂きの刑に処された。だが彼の法は残り、秦の統一の土台となった。
body.en:
Born a prince of Wey, [[p:商鞅|Shang Yang]] found no place in Wei and went west to serve Duke Xiao of Qin. In two rounds of reform, in 356 and 350 BC, he turned Qin into the strongest of the Warring States.

He grouped households in fives and tens and made the crime of one the crime of all; gave rank for heads taken in battle ([[a:qin_rank|ranks for heads]]) and struck royal kinsmen without merit from the clan register; doubled the tax on households with two grown sons, so that families split up. He moved the capital to Xianyang, merged the villages into forty-one counties governed by the king's own magistrates, redrew the field boundaries and made measures and weights the same everywhere — a bronze measure of his still survives.

To make people trust the law he set up a thirty-foot pole at the south gate of the capital and offered ten gold to whoever moved it to the north gate. No one believed him; he raised it to fifty. A man moved it — and was paid.

When Duke Xiao died in 338 BC Shang Yang, hated by many, had to flee. At an inn the keeper turned him away: "By Lord Shang's law, whoever lodges a guest without papers is punished." "So the maker of the law is caught by it," Shang Yang sighed. He was taken and torn apart by chariots — but his laws remained, the foundation of Qin's unification.

body.ja:
前355年頃、小国の韓の昭侯は、もとは身分の低い役人であった[[p:申不害]]を宰相とした。申不害が説いたのは「術」——君主が臣下を操る技である。

君主は自分の好みや考えを見せてはならない。見せれば臣下はそれに合わせて取り入る。役目 (名) を与え、その働き (実) が役目に合っているかを見比べて賞罰を決める (名を循いて実を責む)。そうすれば臣下は君主を欺けない。

申不害が生きている間の十五年、韓はよく治まり、兵は強く、攻めてくる国はなかったと『史記』は書く。のちに韓の公子[[p:韓非]]は、[[p:商鞅]]の「法」、申不害の「術」、慎到の「勢」を合わせて法家の考えをまとめ、その書は秦の始皇帝を感嘆させた。
body.en:
Around 355 BC Marquis Zhao of the small state of Han made [[p:申不害|Shen Buhai]], once a minor official, his chief minister. Shen taught shu — "method", the art by which a ruler handles his ministers.

A ruler must never show his likes or his thoughts, or his ministers will flatter him to suit them. He gives each a title and checks whether the performance matches the title, rewarding and punishing accordingly. Then no minister can deceive him.

For the fifteen years of Shen's life, says the Records of the Grand Historian, Han was well governed, its army strong, and no one attacked it. Later [[p:韓非|Han Fei]], a prince of Han, joined [[p:商鞅|Shang Yang]]'s law, Shen Buhai's method and Shen Dao's power into one Legalist teaching — a book that moved the First Emperor of Qin to admiration.

title.ja: 度量衡・文字の統一と郡県
title.en: One measure, one script, one realm

body.ja:
前221年に天下を一つにした秦は、国ごとにばらばらだったものを一つにそろえた。長さ・容積・重さの単位 (度量衡)、文字、銭、そして車の車軸の幅 (車同軌)。轍の幅がそろえば、どの国の道でも同じ車が走れる。

文字は[[p:李斯]]らが整えた「小篆」に統一された。銭は円い形に四角い穴の「半両銭」となり、のちの東アジアの銭の形のもとになった。秦の分銅や升には、統一を告げる始皇帝の詔が刻まれ、それが今も各地から見つかっている。

封建の諸侯は置かず、天下を三十六の郡に分け、郡には守 (長官)・尉 (軍)・監 (監察) を中央から送った。博士の淳于越が昔のように王の子弟を封じるよう説くと、李斯は「古を引いて今を誹る」と退け、やがて焚書へとつながっていく。

秦は十五年で滅んだが、郡県の仕組みと統一された文字は、その後二千年の中国の形となった。
body.en:
Having united the realm in 221 BC, Qin made one of everything that had differed from state to state: units of length, volume and weight, the script, the coinage — and even the width of cart axles, so that the same cart could run in the ruts of any road.

The script was standardised as the "small seal" worked out by [[p:李斯|Li Si]] and others. Coins became round with a square hole — the banliang, ancestor of East Asian coinage. Qin weights and measures carry the First Emperor's edict of unification, and they turn up all over China to this day.

There were no fief-holding lords: the realm was divided into thirty-six commanderies, each with a governor, a military commandant and an inspector sent from the centre. When the scholar Chunyu Yue urged that the emperor's sons be given fiefs as of old, Li Si rejected "using the past to slander the present" — the road to the burning of the books.

Qin fell in fifteen years, but the commanderies and the common script shaped China for the next two thousand.
